title: Pixel art reskin experiments with AI
author: HugoDzz
selftext: Trying things on the spritefusion edit mode. Not perfect, but promising! Let me know if you’d like me to try on some of your sprites.

comments.author: _Wilbraham
comments.body: Why did you not fix Pool Party before posting this?

comments.author: MrBadBoyWorldwide
comments.body: Unfortunately movement absolutely kills it. Now we need all these outfits in 8 different directions with animations. Unless you want a basic left to right

replies.author: No_Bass_8636
replies.body: Yeah the best way seems to be 2d gen>3d model gen>export to 2.5d directional sprites from blender etc

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body:
Yeah agree, that's still baby steps I'm exploring. So far it can already do the 8 directions (or any pose) with solid consistency (not perfect, some are tricker than others). I put a doc on that [here](https://www.spritefusion.com/docs/pixel-art-generator/edit-your-pixel-art).

https://preview.redd.it/dyqiboiw4hmh1.png?width=1748&format=png&auto=webp&s=d093b612a696337ef275db1505e962c4eabf9154

replies.author: MrBadBoyWorldwide
replies.body: Yes, but once you add in the ability to swap items / use different weapons. Your number of required sprites moves from 900 or so to like 10,000 images.

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body:
Another example for pose change + animation. Basically my workflow here was: take the base sprite (in the main post example above), ask for an armor, ask for a walk pose, and animate for walk.
